<!-- pr-reviewer: 591f758296179c34ffd3d78d73189ad508fcc4a0 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One pinning test fails when the PR is merged with the current `main`.

### Scope

The PR changes the display mesh of the simulated tool only (`JudgedOutline::mesh`, used by `SimToolCache` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/world.rs`). The collision checks, the verify step, the post gate and the posted G-code do not read this mesh. I found no change to posted G-code, to a gouge or collision check, or to stock simulation. I ran two mutations anyway.

### What looks good

- `with_drawn` refuses a drawn point outside every band at its height, and a stored cutter that is wider or longer than the judged one. The picture cannot be wider than the check.
- A machine-default holder and an imported STL/STEP body keep the band drawing.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` in non-test code. The new refusal has a name and a message.
- The cache key (`JudgedOutline` equality) now includes `drawn`, so a profile edit rebuilds the mesh. The undo test pins this.
- The moved test keeps the `#[test]` count. A decision file is present. `sim_tool_body.rs` is 371 lines.

### Results (built locally, Linux, trial merge with `main` e3f7d122b)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `sim_tool_drawn_holder` | **3 passed, 1 failed** |
| `sim_tool_body` | 6 passed |
| `tool_body_judged` | 8 passed |
| `tool_neck_laws` | 4 passed |
| `tool_spun_profile` | 7 passed |
| `holder_library` | 12 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app --lib --test sim_tool_drawn_holder --test sim_tool_body -D warnings` | clean |

```
---- a_drawn_cone_is_drawn_as_a_cone_and_judged_as_its_enclosing_band stdout ----
panicked at crates/app/tests/sim_tool_drawn_holder.rs:137:5:
the judged shank is the enclosing Ø60
```

On the PR head alone (591f758), `sim_tool_drawn_holder` passes 4 of 4. The failure comes from `main`.

`clippy --all-targets` does not compile on `main` because of `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs`. The PR does not touch that file. Issue #2244 tracks it.

Mutations (local, not pushed):

1. Disable the drawn-point band check in `with_drawn`: `checks_verify_and_simulation_read_one_holder_shape` fails at line 192 (`Ok(..)` in place of `Err(PastJudged)`). Red, as expected.
2. Skip `with_drawn` in `for_operation`: all 4 tests in `sim_tool_drawn_holder` fail. Red, as expected.

### Requested before merge

1. `crates/app/tests/sim_tool_drawn_holder.rs:137`: PR #2207 (fix for #2199, commit 2aafba7eb) merged to `main`. It changes `HolderProfile::enclose` to strict interior bounds, so a band that only touches the shank top no longer widens `shank_d`. The judged shank is now the stored shank, not Ø60. Merge `main` into the branch and update this assertion to the new judged value.
2. Read again the shank part of the change after that merge. With #2207, `judged.cutter` and the `stored` cutter are probably the same for these cases. Then the shank substitution in `with_drawn` and `for_operation` (`crates/app/src/sim_tool_body.rs`, the `stored` argument) has no effect. Keep it as a guard or remove it, but make the text agree with `main`:
   - the PR body ("The judged record widens the shank to each band that touches the shank top");
   - `docs/decisions/2176-sim-draws-drawn-holder.md` (the paragraph on `HolderProfile::enclose`, inclusive bounds);
   - the "Follow-up" section of the PR body, which #2207 already did.

### Notes (not blocking)

- `for_operation` uses `.unwrap_or_default()` when `JudgedOutline::new(&tool, &stack)` fails. The result is safe (the wider judged shank is drawn), but the failure is not logged.
- `with_drawn` checks the drawn vertices, not the segments between them. This is correct while the bands come from the same outline, as they do here.
- The PR changes no file in `crates/ui`, so the screenshot rule does not apply. A before/after picture of the issue's holder would help the maintainer.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. Merged main and corrected the cone test for #2207's strict interior bounds. `a_drawn_cone_is_drawn_as_a_cone_and_judged_as_its_enclosing_band` now checks the stored shank diameter. The old Ø60 assertion fails. The restored test passes.
2. Kept the stored-cutter substitution as a defensive guard. Corrected the code comments, decision file, and PR body. Removed the completed follow-up. The cone test and `checks_verify_and_simulation_read_one_holder_shape` check equal stored and judged cutters. Disabling the width guard makes the second test fail. Restoring it makes all four drawn-holder tests pass.

Head: f051671486bc97a4970d944cb78fc91950f1b531.

Quick gate: all seven steps pass. Clippy for all camcraft-app targets is clean.

I returned the PR to draft before the push because this head needs review. Please re-review this head.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f051671486bc97a4970d944cb78fc91950f1b531 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Both findings from the earlier review are addressed. No blocking findings remain.

The review used the current upstream `AGENTS.md`. Local verification used `.claude/worktrees/review-2179` on Linux. The trial merge with upstream/main `4e0b9abefcb225595d47d9c69a2482d6359b190f` was already up to date.

- The cone test now checks the stored shank diameter. It also checks that the stored and judged cutter outlines agree.
- The code comments, decision file and PR body describe strict interior bounds. They retain the stored-cutter substitution as a defensive guard.
- The display reads the landed outline. The checks retain the judged bands. Profile edits rebuild the cached mesh, and undo restores the outline.

This received a safety-tier review. The changed mesh supplies the viewport display. I found no change to posted G-code, collision verdicts or stock removal. No golden files changed. I read the moved cone assertions line by line. No `crates/ui` files changed, so the before/after screenshot requirement does not apply.

Local results:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app --no-run` | Pass |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | All seven steps pass |
| App library | 356 passed, 1 ignored |
| `sim_lathe_body` | 5 passed |
| `sim_tool_body` | 6 passed |
| `sim_tool_drawn_holder` | 4 passed |
| `tool_body_judged` | 8 passed |
| `tool_neck_laws` | 4 passed |
| `tool_spun_profile` | 7 passed |
| `holder_library` | 12 passed |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Clean |

I repeated these mutations locally:

1. Restore the old Ø60 shank assertion. The cone test fails at `crates/app/tests/sim_tool_drawn_holder.rs:137`: actual diameter 6, expected 60. After restoration, all four tests pass.
2. Disable the stored-cutter width refusal. `checks_verify_and_simulation_read_one_holder_shape` fails at `crates/app/tests/sim_tool_drawn_holder.rs:199`: `Ok` replaces `Err(PastJudged)`. After restoration, all four tests pass.

All mutation edits were restored. The worktree has no tracked changes. The UI crate and GUI rendering were not exercised. The PR's draft state stays unchanged.

Requested before merge: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
Merged by the order of the maintainer of 2026-11-16. No second safety-floor review was made.
